transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because people keep acting like I’m making something out of nothing, but I’ve been looking into what happened around my father’s death, and it doesn’t add up.

Everyone says the hospital records and the donation emails are consistent, but when I compare the timestamps and notice certain attachments are missing, and then I ask people in the community simple questions and they suddenly get evasive… it’s pretty clear to me someone is hiding what really happened.

I work with systems, so I’m used to patterns and logs and things lining up or not lining up. And this doesn’t line up. I know that probably sounds like I’ve been obsessing over details, but the details are the whole point.
Can you tell me more about what you believe actually happened with your father's death and why you think others are hiding the truth?

I mean… what I think happened is that the story they’re giving me isn’t the full story. I’m not saying I have every single piece, but when I look at the hospital records and then the donation emails, people keep saying they line up, but they don’t. Not really.

There are timestamps that don’t make sense, and some attachments that should be there just aren’t. And then when I ask people in the community about it—people who should be able to answer basic questions—they get weirdly careful, like they’re choosing every word.

It reminds me of when I’m reviewing system logs at work, actually. You can tell when something has been cleaned up after the fact, even if it looks fine to someone else. Sorry, that’s probably not the point, but that’s how I notice things. So to me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
Do you believe that certain people or groups are working together in secret to cover up what happened to your father?

I don’t know if I’d say “groups” exactly, like some dramatic thing with meetings in a basement or whatever. But… yes, I do think certain people are coordinating, or at least they know more than they’re saying.

Because everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails line up, and they just don’t. When I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then the way some community members dodge simple questions, it’s obvious to me someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.

It’s like at work when a system report looks clean on the surface, but the logs tell you something was altered later. Sorry, I know that’s kind of a technical comparison, but that’s how I see it. Something has been covered up.
Do you think this cover-up is limited to what happened with your father, or do you believe it's part of something bigger or more widespread?

I don’t know if I’d call it widespread. I’m not trying to say there’s some huge network behind everything. It’s more… around my father’s death specifically, that’s where I keep seeing the inconsistencies.

Like, everyone tells me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then certain people in the community suddenly avoiding my questions, it’s obvious to me someone is hiding what really happened.

I mean, I spend all day looking at systems where one small mismatch can show the whole process was altered, so maybe I notice things other people don’t. Sorry, that’s a bit of a tangent. But no, I’m mainly focused on what happened with my father. That’s where the cover-up is.
Do you have any idea why you think these people are hiding the truth about your father's death?

I think they’re hiding it because if the real timeline came out, someone would look responsible. Maybe not in a criminal way—I don’t know—but responsible enough that they’d rather keep everything looking neat.

Everyone keeps saying the hospital records and donation emails line up, but when I compare the timestamps and the missing attachments, they just don’t. And then certain people in the community avoid my questions, like they suddenly have to be careful. That’s what makes it obvious to me something is being covered up.

It’s like when a system gets patched after an incident and the report says everything was normal, but the logs show gaps. Sorry, I keep going back to work examples. But that’s why. I think the truth would make someone look bad.
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, such as hearing voices or believing things that others don’t seem to understand, even before you started looking into your father’s death?

I don’t think I was hearing voices or anything like that, if that’s what you mean. Before all this, I mean, I had normal thoughts, work stress, family stuff… sometimes I’d get stuck on details, but that’s kind of my job too, you know? If a timestamp is off by even a little bit in a system, it can mean the whole record is wrong.

But the thing with my father—this isn’t just me having a strange thought. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails line up, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then the way certain community members avoid my questions, it’s obvious to me someone is hiding what really happened around his death.

So, no, not before that. This started because there were things that didn’t add up.
Have there ever been times when you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or were more irritable than usual for several days or longer?

I’m not sure. I mean, I get irritable sometimes, but I think most people do when they’re not being listened to or when something keeps looping in your head.

As far as energy or needing less sleep for days… I don’t really know how to answer that. My sleep can get thrown off when I’m trying to figure something out, like if I’m comparing details and I lose track of time, but I wouldn’t say I suddenly feel amazing or anything. It’s more like I get stuck on a problem. At work that happens too—if a system issue is hard to trace, you can stay up later than you meant to.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed that in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.

Have there been times when you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to understand or agree with, even when there wasn’t clear evidence to support it, and not related to your father’s death?

Not really outside of that… I mean, I know you’re asking “not related,” but that’s the one that stands out because it’s not just a feeling to me.

People keep acting like I’m making connections where there aren’t any, but the hospital records, the donation emails, the timestamps, the missing attachments—those things don’t line up the way everyone says they do. And then when certain people in the community start avoiding basic questions, it’s hard not to see that as… deliberate.

Sorry, I know I’m circling back. But no, I can’t think of another separate thing like that. It’s this situation with my father where everyone else says it’s fine, and to me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
Do you ever believe something is definitely true, even though you can’t explain why and others don’t see it the same way, and it stays on your mind even when people try to convince you otherwise?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t think it’s just “for no reason,” though. That’s the part people keep missing.

With my father’s death, I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, like it’s settled. But when I sit down and compare the timestamps, and then there are missing attachments, and then certain people in the community suddenly don’t want to answer basic questions… I don’t know how I’m supposed to ignore that.

It stays on my mind, yes. Even when people say I’m overthinking it. I work with systems, so I’m used to small mismatches meaning something bigger is wrong. And this feels like that. To me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened.

Even though you’ve described how you came to believe there’s a cover-up around your father’s death, if someone were to show you clear evidence that the hospital records and emails are complete and accurate, and that people are just avoiding your questions out of discomfort or misunderstanding, would you be willing to consider that there’s no deliberate hiding of the truth?

I’d… I’d look at it, yes. I’m not trying to be unreasonable. I work with records and systems, so if something is complete, it should be able to hold up when you check it.

But I guess my problem is that people keep saying “clear evidence,” and then when I actually compare the timestamps or ask about the missing attachments, suddenly it’s like nobody wants to talk about that part. And I’ve seen that kind of thing at work too, where everyone says the log is fine until you notice one field that doesn’t match and then the whole story changes.

So… willing to consider it, maybe. But if the same gaps are still there, and people keep avoiding simple questions, then no, I don’t think I could just accept that nothing was being hidden. To me it still feels obvious that someone is covering up what really happened with my father.

Even if someone were to show you complete and consistent hospital records and emails, and explain why the attachments are missing and why people are avoiding your questions, would you still believe there is a cover-up around your father’s death?

I mean… if it was actually complete and consistent, I’d have to look at it. I’m not trying to just reject things because they don’t fit what I think.

But it’s hard for me to imagine, because that’s what people already keep saying—“the records line up,” “the emails are fine”—and then when I compare the timestamps, or ask why certain attachments are missing, or why people in the community suddenly get weird and won’t answer basic questions, it doesn’t feel explained. It feels like the explanation is always just enough to get me to stop asking.

So… honestly, yes, I think I would still have a hard time believing there wasn’t something being hidden. Maybe that sounds stubborn, but to me those little gaps matter. In my work, when a system has mismatched logs, you don’t just say, “Well, someone explained it,” and move on. You keep digging.

So yes… I think I’d still believe there’s a cover-up around what really happened with my father.

So yes… I think I’d still believe there’s a cover-up around what really happened with my father.

The differential also includes Schizotypal Disorder (F21), given the odd beliefs and suspiciousness, though without prominent functional decline or interpersonal withdrawal. The possibility of a Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (F23.2) remains due to the presence of what appear to be delusions, though there is insufficient evidence for a full schizophrenic syndrome (e.g., hallucinations, disorganized thinking, negative symptoms), making F20.0, F25.0, and F23.0 less likely. No features of bipolar disorder or mania were endorsed, ruling out F25.0.
